questions.question: She is reading a book, ______?
questions.explanation: Affirmative statement with auxiliary 'is' takes negative tag 'isn't she?'.

questions.question: You don't like coffee, ______?
questions.explanation: Negative statement with 'don't' takes positive tag 'do you?'.

questions.question: Let's go for a walk, ______?
questions.explanation: Statements beginning with 'Let's' always take the question tag 'shall we?'.

questions.question: Close the door, ______?
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences (requests/orders) take 'will you?' or 'won't you?' as tag.

questions.question: I am right, ______?
questions.explanation: Affirmative 'I am' takes the tag 'aren't I?' in standard English.

questions.question: I am not late, ______?
questions.explanation: Negative 'I am not' takes the positive tag 'am I?'.

questions.question: Neither of them came, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Neither' makes the clause negative, taking pronoun 'they' and positive tag 'did they?'.

questions.question: Nobody phoned, ______?
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronoun 'Nobody' takes plural pronoun 'they' and positive auxiliary 'did they?'.

questions.question: Few people know the answer, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Few' has a negative meaning, so it takes a positive tag 'do they?'.

questions.question: A few students attended the class, ______?
questions.explanation: 'A few' has a positive meaning, so it takes a negative tag 'didn't they?'.

questions.question: Little progress has been made, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Little' has a negative meaning without 'a', so it takes the positive tag 'has it?'.

questions.question: A little progress has been made, ______?
questions.explanation: 'A little' is positive in meaning, so it takes the negative tag 'hasn't it?'.

questions.question: Barking dogs seldom bite, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Seldom' is semi-negative; 'dogs' is plural, requiring 'do they?'.

questions.question: He hardly ever goes there, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' makes the sentence negative, requiring a positive tag 'does he?'.

questions.question: She scarcely uttered a word, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely' conveys a negative idea; past tense 'uttered' takes 'did she?'.

questions.question: Everyone has arrived, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' takes plural pronoun 'they' in question tags, requiring plural verb 'haven't they?'.

questions.question: Somebody stole my purse, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Somebody' takes pronoun 'they' in the tag; past tense 'stole' takes 'didn't they?'.

questions.question: Nothing was said, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Nothing' refers to a thing (it) and makes the sentence negative, so the tag is 'was it?'.

questions.question: Everything looks fine, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Everything' takes singular neuter pronoun 'it'; positive present takes 'doesn't it?'.

questions.question: Don't make noise, ______?
questions.explanation: Negative imperative 'Don't...' takes positive tag 'will you?'.

questions.question: Have some tea, ______?
questions.explanation: Imperative offer takes 'will you?'.

questions.question: Let us do this work, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Let us' (allowing us) takes 'will you?' whereas 'Let's' (suggestion) takes 'shall we?'.

questions.question: There is some water in the glass, ______?
questions.explanation: Sentences beginning with introductory 'there' retain 'there' in the tag: 'isn't there?'.

questions.question: There are no problems, ______?
questions.explanation: Negative sentence with 'no' and introductory 'there' takes positive tag 'are there?'.

questions.question: One should obey one's elders, ______?

questions.question: He used to live here, ______?

questions.question: She ought to help him, ______?

questions.question: He dare not do that, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Dare not' is a negative modal auxiliary, so it takes 'dare he?'.

questions.question: She dares to challenge him, ______?
questions.explanation: Here 'dares' is an ordinary verb in present simple, taking 'doesn't she?'.

questions.question: You need not go there, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Need not' functions as a modal auxiliary, taking positive tag 'need you?'.

questions.question: He needs money, ______?

questions.question: You had better leave now, ______?

questions.question: You would rather stay, ______?
questions.explanation: 'Would rather' takes 'wouldn't you?'.
